title: The sprint skill's run step submits land, stage-back and sync as jobs, follows them with the Monitor tool and goes on to the next ready item
goal: the kb-sprint skill (in the clone and in the plugin's copy) tells the orchestrator, when python3 _tools/kbjob.py ping exits 0, to submit each landing, stage-back and sync --push with kbjob.py submit OP ID --by claude-<8 hex>, to follow it with one Monitor call on kbjob.py follow JOB (a line per move; a waiting-merge line is the cue to run backlog.py merge ID or tell the operator) or a background shell on the same command, and to go on at once with dispatching and claiming the next ready items and answering gates, instead of one background land ID > log per landing and a coord.py wait; a follow that ends with exit 4 is run again with its --since; the existing path stays for a host where ping exits 1 and for a headless worker; .claude/settings.json allows python3 _tools/kbjob.py submit, follow, status, log, cancel, ping and ensure and never serve or login-item; kb/_self/backlog.md describes the job step beside the run states

run: import sys; t=[open(p).read() for p in (".claude/skills/kb-sprint/SKILL.md","skills/sprint/SKILL.md")]; assert all("kbjob.py submit" in x and "kbjob.py follow" in x and "Monitor" in x and "kbjob.py ping" in x for x in t), "skill text lacks the job step"; assert all("land ID > <scratch>/land.log" not in x for x in t), "the background land log recipe is still the way"

notes: Premise: what the skill says today (kb-sprint SKILL.md:62 step 4.4 and :57): start land in the background with the log in the scratch directory and wait with coord.py wait --kind progress --item IDS as a background command; the orchestrator is told when it exits. So the wait is already a background command and the session may do other things; what it cannot do is outlive the session, keep the log (land removes the scratch directory: ST-vbwxcncr, ST-kios45l7) or see more than the run state's moves. Measured 2026-11-08 (kb/_querylog/ops, real items, 2026-10-02..11-08, 376 orchestrator-like session files): only 66 of 964 matched landings were a foreground call that ended with the land (7%); but 285 foreground calls of coord.py of 30 s or more (median 212 s, max 580 s) added up to 20.8 h of 104.7 h session wall (20%), 112 backlog.py calls of 30 s or more (median 58 s) 2.2 h, 103 tests.py calls (median 41 s) 1.4 h and 56 kbgit.py calls (median 88 s) 1.6 h: the orchestrator blocks in the wait call itself. The step changes the wait into a Monitor line per move so the model's turn is free for the next dispatch. Protected paths: .claude/settings.json is an agents-rule path, so this story's landing is staged back by the orchestrator (ST-qs27ongb) and its start gate may be held; the skill copy in skills/sprint/ is the plugin's, kept by hand beside the clone's (plugin.md). The behaviour is proven by the first sprint that runs it; the checks prove the text and the CLI it names. Complement: EP-nij36lt7 (run states in coord, waited on by the orchestrator) is the item-level sibling; the job states are the operation-level ones, and the skill reads both.
